Viewport context menus

Verified causes and historical behavior

Commit c20005054a36 (7 February 2026) introduced selection shortcuts on empty space. Its element-hit early returns were intentional: it did not implement an individual fixture editor menu. a0e65b3eed42 (20 July) extended that design to trusses. Consequently the old 2D handler explicitly skipped a fixture/truss hit. This was missing functionality, rather than a menu ownership regression.

74e7aff35362 (1 August) extracted the 3D selection-submenu policy and guarded unavailable/empty selection menus. Its selectionObjectHit suppressed only the selection shortcuts. Render style and Export image remained available on hits and when picking was unavailable. Both right-up event bindings existed; stack menu lifetime and transferred submenu ownership were valid.

A separate verified suppression path existed before menu construction: OnCaptureLost called NavigationSession::End(), which deliberately retained HasMoved(). OnRightUp returned on that flag without consuming/resetting it. There was no right-down binding to start a fresh click. Losing capture after camera movement could therefore suppress every subsequent right-click until another gesture cleared the flag. The navigation policy extraction (b6dd4d61) retained this path; this analysis does not attribute the original introduction of the defect to that refactor.

Capture loss now resets navigation completely. Each viewer has a separate right-button gesture tracker: press resets it, motion beyond three logical pixels suppresses the popup even if the pointer returns, and release consumes it. Active navigation/selection gestures block it. Escape and capture loss cancel it. Placement and line-point right-click cancellation take precedence. No right-button camera navigation binding has been added.

Ownership and selection

viewer_common/context_menu_model.* replaces the old 3D-only action policy. It has no wxWidgets, OpenGL, ConfigManager or renderer dependency. Typed UUID hits, effective selection, normal click/group membership, interaction state and capabilities produce ordered actions and a selection replacement decision. The original clicked UUID remains the individual editing target.

Each viewport keeps its normal picking adapter. The 2D handler uses ResolvePickForScope and Viewer2DInteractionScopePolicy; 3D uses the same QueryHoverUuid/QueryHoverUuidAcrossTables paths as ordinary selection. Content scale conversion, visibility and depth confirmation remain owned by those picking services. There is no stale hover fallback. Cross-table actions retain the current preference and picking priority. Merely requesting a menu does not reload GDTFs or rebuild geometry.

gui/viewport_context_menu.* constructs and dispatches the wx menu. Runtime IDs are held by wxWindowIDRef until dispatch completes, avoiding fixed-range collisions and leaked reservations. Submenus transfer ownership to their parent. On an already-selected effective member, no selection setters run: typed membership, direct groups, chronology and highlights stay intact. An unselected hit uses the existing group-expansion policy, with the configured movement preferences, and publishes through RefreshAfterToolSelectionUpdate and SetSceneSelection. Selection-only menu preparation creates no scene Undo entry. Empty space preserves selection and exposes the existing type/position shortcuts.

Intentional viewport differences remain: only 3D offers Render style and Export image; 2D camera-only Layout editors keep scene interaction disabled. The 3D renderer currently has fixture/truss/object picking targets, without a dedicated hoist pick target. Hoists are directly contextual in 2D and participate in mixed selections/groups and supported collective actions in both viewers. This change does not introduce another 3D picking backend.

Reused editing and command contracts

  • Fixture and truss editors reuse the existing table activation handlers and dialogs. UUIDs resolve through stable item identities at invocation, including sorted tables and inactive notebook pages. Editors retain their validation, resource ownership, refresh and history paths.
  • Primitive editing is offered only when the existing primitive/screen/pipe editor can handle the object. The capability query uses that editor's actual classification logic. Conversion invokes the existing scene-to-truss handler and command with the clicked source UUID, preserving its same-model scope.
  • Position Tool focuses the existing panel. Group, Ungroup, Copy and Delete dispatch existing application commands with their current validation/history behavior. Unsupported direct-group-only destructive actions are omitted.
  • Both viewport double-click patch handlers now share viewport_scene_editing. Numeric validation precedes acceptance; SetFixturePrimaryPatch prepares a private candidate and preserves canonical DMX side assignments. Failure and no-op publish nothing. Success uses GuiProjectMutationHost for one snapshot, change notification and Undo/Redo, then the existing tool scene refresh. The prior handlers directly wrote Fixture.address/ID without history and bypassed canonical assignment validation.

No alignment implementation or controls are added. A future action enum can carry Align Top/Bottom/Left/Right/Center Horizontally/Center Vertically and forward to the existing alignment command IDs/service. Applicability must come from that service; toolbar reference chronology, work plane and insertion-point policy remain authoritative.

Validation

Viewer3DContextMenuModel now tests the shared model: UUID targeting, preserved multi-selection order, group membership, all categories, omitted unsupported editors, empty-space capabilities, active interactions and drag recovery. Existing selection, grouping, command, clipboard, alignment and navigation suites remain relevant contract tests.

The native smoke uses production application objects and real wx popup loops:

cmake --build build/wsl-x64-debug --target Perastage viewer3d_context_menu_model_test
xvfb-run -a -s '-screen 0 1600x1000x24' \
  env LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 python3 tests/run_viewport_regression_smoke.py \
  build/wsl-x64-debug --source tests/viewport_context_menu_smoke.cpp

It observes menu-open events, dismisses with native Escape, exercises fixture and patch editor cancellation, selection chronology, cross-table targeting, hidden-fixture exclusion, right-drag suppression/recovery, actual camera movement and capture-loss recovery. It verifies atomic validated patch Undo/Redo and Group dispatch/Undo through the production command handler. Linux wxGTK/Xvfb checks do not establish Windows/macOS native popup behavior; those platforms still need their native checks.
